title: Never trust an error's name.
description: An error's name is writable, so it can carry anything into a log. How our shared ops package logs only a fixed list of error types, and fails safely.
lede: We thought logging only an error’s type was the safe choice. Then we remembered that the type is a string anyone can set.
summary: Lessons from @ideasquared/ops: a fixed list of error types for logs, a logger that can never change a response, and an authoriser whose errors never reach the caller.
